cards.name: Craquelure
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that renders the rasterized artwork as if painted onto a high-relief plaster surface, covered with a fine embossed network of cracks that follows the artwork's contours. Flat vector fills turn into a crazed, aged-paint or old-ceramic surface of lit raised plates separated by dark crack lines.
use_for: aged or antique poster background
cracked-paint, distressed retro label or badge
old fresco / glazed-ceramic surface on a flat illustration
worn texture on large headline shapes
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB) or do the look in Photoshop.
Small type and thin strokes: the crack relief breaks them up and kills legibility.
Print logos that must stay scalable and editable: the cracks are raster at the Document Raster Effects resolution; use a vector grunge texture as an opacity mask instead.

Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send Crack Spacing / Crack Depth / Crack Brightness: a scripted apply runs without the Photoshop parameter block, so it renders with the dialog's last-used values; the gallery route (see scripting) carries chosen values (harvest render of that route: mean diff vs plain 1.161).

params.name: Crack Spacing
params.does: distance between cracks: small values give fine crazing, large values big plates with few cracks
params.typical: 15 (dialog value at harvest) fine crazing; 50-90 large, clearly readable plates

params.name: Crack Depth
params.does: how deeply the cracks are embossed, i.e. how strong their shadow and highlight are

params.name: Crack Brightness
params.does: lightness of the crack relief; lower values give darker, higher-contrast crack lines
params.typical: 9 (dialog value at harvest); 3-5 for darker, more obvious cracks

pairs_with: Effect > Distort & Transform > Roughen for worn edges that match the aged surface
Effect > Texture > Texturizer for an extra canvas weave under the cracks
Document Raster Effects Settings (crack spacing is in pixels: the same value looks finer at higher ppi)
cards.scripting: item.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="PSAdapter_plugin_Crql"><Dict data="I dataSize 84 I PrevDres 300 B go 1"/></LiveEffect>') applies the live effect, but Crack Spacing / Crack Depth / Crack Brightness live in the binary 'data' descriptor that Dict data cannot carry, so a scripted apply runs without them (it then renders with the dialog's last-used values). For chosen values: select the item and app.executeMenuCommand('Live PSAdapter_plugin_Crql') (opens the 'Craquelure (100%)' dialog with the last-used values, needs OK), or save a hand-made version as a Graphic Style and doc.graphicStyles.getByName('<style>').applyTo(item). Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).
cards.cost: medium: rasterizes the object at the Document Raster Effects resolution (PrevDres 300 recorded) through the Filter Gallery; slows redraw on large artwork
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live effect in the Appearance panel (double-click to edit); Object > Expand Appearance bakes it into an embedded image

review.changes: PS-doc dialog ranges removed from params.does (not in the harvest, which has no min/max); scripting / avoid no longer claim the scripted route renders 'fallback settings' (batch: the Photoshop parameters are not sent and their rendering is unverified); Crack Brightness typical drops the '(light)' reading of the harvested 9 (not measured); equivalents.CDR added: Effects/Texture/Elephant Skin (aged crease network, the CDR card maps back to Craquelure)

verified.note: A fine embossed network of dark cracks covers the photo, the strip and the ramp, following the contours like crazed paint on plaster, as the card describes.

cards.name: Grain
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that adds texture grain to the rasterized artwork; Grain Type sets its character: fine Regular or Soft noise, Sprinkles, Clumped, Contrasty, Enlarged, Stippled dots, Horizontal or Vertical streaks, or Speckle. Flat vector fills pick up a noisy, printed or film-like speckle while keeping their colours.
use_for: risograph / printed-paper feel on a flat poster illustration
vintage film texture on a background shape
dithering a large gradient so it bands less
Horizontal or Vertical type for a scanline / brushed-metal streak texture
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB) or do the look in Photoshop.
Small type and hairlines: grain eats thin edges.
Artwork re-output at another size or ppi: grain is pixel based and changes size with the Document Raster Effects resolution; for a scalable texture use a vector pattern swatch.

Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send Intensity / Contrast / Grain Type: a scripted apply runs without the Photoshop parameter block, so it renders with the dialog's last-used values; the gallery route (see scripting) carries chosen values (harvest render of that route: mean diff vs plain 2.404).

params.name: Contrast
params.does: contrast of the grain against the artwork

params.name: Grain Type
params.does: shape and pattern of the grain (noise, dots, clumps, streaks, speckle)
params.typical: Clumped (dialog value at harvest) or Regular for film grain; Horizontal / Vertical for streaks

pairs_with: Appearance panel: put Grain on a second fill set to Multiply or Overlay at lower opacity to keep the base colour clean
Effect > Artistic > Cutout for flat posterized colour under the grain
Document Raster Effects Settings (grain size is in pixels)

cards.name: Mosaic Tiles
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that draws the rasterized artwork as if built from small, slightly irregular chips or tiles with sunken grout lines between them; the artwork's colours and detail stay inside each tile, so the shapes read through a tiled, embossed surface (unlike a flat-colour pixel mosaic).
use_for: tiled wall or floor surface on a poster graphic
ceramic mosaic treatment of a logo shape for a signage mock-up
crafty texture on large background shapes
bathroom / pool-tile theme for packaging artwork
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB) or do the look in Photoshop.
Small type and thin strokes: grout lines cut through them.
When flat single-colour cells are wanted: use Effect > Texture > Patchwork (squares filled with the predominant colour) or Photoshop's Filter > Pixelate > Mosaic.

Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send Tile Size / Grout Width / Lighten Grout: a scripted apply runs without the Photoshop parameter block, so it renders with the dialog's last-used values; the gallery route (see scripting) carries chosen values (harvest render of that route: mean diff vs plain 1.544).

params.name: Tile Size
params.does: size of each tile in pixels

params.name: Grout Width
params.does: width of the grout lines between tiles

params.name: Lighten Grout
params.does: how much the grout lines between the tiles are lightened (higher = lighter grout, by the dialog's name; the harvest did not measure it)
params.typical: 9 (dialog value at harvest); 1-3 for darker grout that reads on light colours

pairs_with: Effect > Stylize > Drop Shadow to lift the tiled shape off the page
Effect > Texture > Grain for dusty, worn tiles
Document Raster Effects Settings (tile size is in pixels)

cards.name: Patchwork
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that breaks the rasterized artwork into a grid of small squares, each filled with the predominant colour of that area, and randomly raises or lowers the squares to fake highlights and shadows; the result looks like needlepoint, cross-stitch or a quilted tile grid. Square Size is in raster pixels: on the 1920-pt photo plate 10 px squares show as a fine grid with a dark relief line under each row, which at a reduced preview reads mostly as horizontal ridges.
use_for: needlepoint / cross-stitch look for a craft-themed poster
quilted or knitted texture on a flat illustration
embossed square-grid texture on background shapes
retro textile badge
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB) or do the look in Photoshop.

Chunky pixel-art squares: Square Size is in pixels at the Document Raster Effects resolution, so at 300 ppi the squares stay small; for big blocks lower that resolution or use Photoshop's Filter > Pixelate > Mosaic.
Small type: squares average away letterforms.

Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send Square Size / Relief: a scripted apply runs without the Photoshop parameter block, so it renders with the dialog's last-used values; the gallery route (see scripting) carries chosen values (harvest render of that route: mean diff vs plain 1.602).

params.name: Square Size
params.does: size of the colour squares in pixels
params.typical: 4 at harvest; 8-10 for clearly visible squares

params.name: Relief
params.does: depth of the random raised / sunken shading of the squares

pairs_with: Effect > Texture > Grain for a fibrous textile finish
Document Raster Effects Settings (lower ppi makes the squares larger relative to the artwork)

cards.name: Stained Glass
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that repaints the rasterized artwork as irregular single-colour polygon cells (a honeycomb / Voronoi pattern) outlined with dark lead borders, with an optional light glow from the centre. The border colour is not a dialog setting (Photoshop uses its foreground colour); the harvest's scripted render in Illustrator showed dark borders around the cells with a lighter centre.
use_for: church-window or art-nouveau glass look on a poster illustration
faceted cell background behind a headline
mosaic-style treatment of a logo shape for a festive card
geometric low-detail stylisation of placed artwork
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB) or do the look in Photoshop.
Small type and thin lines: cells and borders destroy them.
When the lead colour must be chosen precisely or stay vector: draw a Voronoi / cell pattern as vector paths instead; the borders here are raster.

Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send Cell Size / Border Thickness / Light Intensity: a scripted apply runs without the Photoshop parameter block, so it renders with the dialog's last-used values; the gallery route (see scripting) carries chosen values (harvest render of that route: mean diff vs plain 4.518).

params.name: Border Thickness
params.does: width of the dark lead lines between cells

params.name: Light Intensity
params.does: strength of the light glowing from the centre of the artwork

pairs_with: Effect > Stylize > Outer Glow for a backlit-window halo
Effect > Texture > Grain for old, frosted glass
Document Raster Effects Settings (cell size is in pixels)

cards.name: Texturizer
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that embosses a surface texture onto the rasterized artwork, lit from a chosen direction: canvas (TxCa) at harvest (the dialog also offers brick, burlap and sandstone, or a loaded texture file). Besides the raised relief with highlights and shadows it mutes the colours: on the photo plate (Canvas, Scaling 200, Relief 30) every saturated colour lost about half its chroma (red 232,32,42 to 199,97,103, orange to tan, pure blue to a greyish blue), and on flat vector art the orange box went tan-brown.
use_for: canvas or paper tooth on a flat illustration
brick or burlap backdrop feel for a poster
printed-on-material look for packaging or label mock-ups
subtle embossed surface on large colour blocks
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB) or do the look in Photoshop.
Small type: the relief roughens edges at strong Relief values.
Custom textures in a pipeline: loading a texture file needs the dialog (Load Texture) and cannot be set from a script.
Scalable vector output: for a resolution-independent texture use a pattern swatch with a blend mode instead.

Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send Texture Type / Scaling / Relief / Light Direction / Invert Texture: a scripted apply runs without the Photoshop parameter block, so it renders with the dialog's last-used values; the gallery route (see scripting) carries chosen values (harvest render of that route: mean diff vs plain 0.825).
colours that must stay saturated (brand colours): the texture relief mutes them by about half; apply it to a copy set to Multiply or Overlay over the original, or lower Relief

params.name: Texture Type
params.does: which texture is embossed (dialog: Brick, Burlap, Canvas, Sandstone or a loaded file); the harvest recorded only the code TxCa (canvas)
params.typical: TxCa (the only code harvested: canvas, the dialog value at harvest)

params.name: Scaling
params.does: size of the texture pattern in percent

params.name: Light Direction
params.does: side the texture is lit from, which sets where emboss highlights fall

pairs_with: Effect > Artistic > Watercolor or Dry Brush for a painted-on-canvas look
Effect > Texture > Grain for extra paper speckle
Document Raster Effects Settings (texture scale is in pixels)

For chosen values: select the item and app.executeMenuCommand('Live PSAdapter_plugin_Txtz') (opens the 'Texturizer (100%)' dialog with the last-used values, needs OK), or save a hand-made version as a Graphic Style and doc.graphicStyles.getByName('<style>').applyTo(item). Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).
cards.cost: medium: emboss pass at the Document Raster Effects resolution (PrevDres 300 recorded) through the Filter Gallery
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live effect in the Appearance panel (double-click to edit); Object > Expand Appearance bakes it into an embedded image

review.changes: PS-doc dialog ranges removed from params.does (not in the harvest, which has no min/max); scripting / avoid no longer claim the scripted route renders 'fallback settings' (batch: the Photoshop parameters are not sent and their rendering is unverified); summary and Texture Type typical say TxCa was the dialog value at harvest, not the default (batch: defaults are the last-used dialog values)

verified.note: The canvas relief is there, but the colours did not stay intact: every colour is muted toward grey (mean chroma 39 against 73 for ref_photo; strip red 232,32,42 -> 199,97,103, orange -> tan 175,120,56, blue 30,63,255 -> 82,99,196), so the 'colours stay intact' claim is wrong; summary and look rewritten.

second_opinion.note: Plate check: sampled all eight strip blocks and the background against ref_photo.png: every saturated colour loses about half its chroma under the embossed canvas, consistent with the first (vector-plate) verdict, where the orange box went tan-brown and the star duller blue; the render route is the dialog-matched gallery route, so the text, not the frame, is at fault.
